intended_object: The general linear group GL_n(I) of a nonunital ring I: the kernel of the reduction map GL_n(ℤ ⋉ I) → GL_n(ℤ), where ℤ ⋉ I is the canonical unitization. This is the standard definition used in algebraic K-theory (e.g. Weibel's K-book, Milnor). Inferred from the docstring and the module.
explanation:
The definition is the kernel of `nonUnitalAugmentation`. That map is `GL n (Unitization ℤ I) → GL n ℤ`, induced entrywise by `Unitization.fstHom`, the ring map ℤ ⊕ I → ℤ that sends (m, a) to m. This kernel is exactly the textbook GL_n(I) := ker(GL_n(ℤ ⊕ I) → GL_n(ℤ)). Its elements are the invertible matrices of the form 1 + x with x ∈ M_n(I), which matches the alternative description by quasi-invertible matrices.

The generality is right. The index type n is any finite type with decidable equality, and I is any nonunital ring, with no commutativity assumed. Using ℤ as the base of the unitization is the canonical choice for a bare nonunital ring.

Mathlib has no general linear group of a nonunital ring. So the definition is faithful and is not a restriction of an existing Mathlib construction.
